claim: Three chunked array teardown routines that free fixed-size chunk blocks from holder slots and then free the holder's inner object, called in a fixed sequence by shared owners.

routines.relation: instruction-identical to 0x5d5a2e0 modulo addresses and call displacements
differs from the other two only in chunk size 0x1f8 instead of 0x200
instruction-identical to 0x5d5a200 modulo addresses and call displacements

owner_sequence.description: Each shared owner calls the three routines in the fixed order 0x5d5a2e0, 0x5d5a270, 0x5d5a200, with rdi from three distinct rbx-relative holders.

shared_gates.null_inner: returns plainly with nothing freed, even though the chunk slots live on the holder
shared_gates.null_slot_pointer_test: none; every visited slot pointer is passed to the sized delete unconditionally
shared_gates.cursor_advance: before the delete call, so frees follow slot order
shared_gates.loop_skipped_exit: tail-jump inner free runs whenever the inner object is non-null, whether the loop ran or was skipped

unknowns: What the holder+0x08 count counts at the source level; only the byte size [holder+0x08] * 8 is pinned.
Why two instruction-identical routines exist for distinct holders; recorded as distinct routines with distinct caller sets, not merged.
The source-level type of the holders and of the chunk blocks; only sizes and offsets are pinned.
What any caller does with a holder before or after the call.
